patches.rationale: Both insurers specify a minimum delay period before baggage delay benefits are payable. Capturing this threshold supports cross-insurer comparison and avoids burying it only in free text/benefits.
patches.description: Minimum checked baggage delay (in hours) before the baggage delay/essential items allowance becomes payable.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: SECTION 6: Delayed Luggage Allowance ... up to $300 per item ... after a 12 hour delay and before the luggage was returned to You. (p34)
D.4.3 Baggage delay during your journey – We cover you if your scheduled transport provider delays your checked-in baggage for more than 12 hours ... up to $1,000 for each person. (p63)

patches.rationale: Both PDSs give concrete rules for specifying items, including per-item eligibility ranges, valuation recency, and per-person aggregate caps. Making the description explicit improves consistent capture.
patches.description: Whether customers can increase item limits or specify items and the total/per-item caps for specified items. Capture any insurer rules such as: eligible per-item value ranges for specifying, valuation requirements (e.g., jewellery/watch valuation from recognised valuers, valuation dated within 24 months), documentation required (original receipts/proof of ownership), and any aggregate cap for all specified items per person (e.g., up to $15,000 total).

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Increase Luggage Item Limit ... For multiple items, the overall increase in limits cannot exceed $15,000. Receipts or valuations (less than 24 months old) must be available if requested. (p34)

D.4.2 Specified items – You can list certain items as a specified item if it has a value of $1,500 to $10,000 for each item; up to $15,000 for all specified items for each person; valuation less than 24 months (specific jeweller valuer requirements). (pp61–62)

patches.rationale: Some insurers cover the insurance excess on the traveller’s own vehicle under driving holidays. Mapping these to the rental_vehicle category via aliases enables consistent benefit normalisation without introducing a new category.
patches.description: Add aliases to the rental_vehicle coverage category to capture own-vehicle excess style benefits.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Domestic Plans – Driving Holidays: Cover for the Insurance Excess on Your Personal Vehicle – $2,500 (Comprehensive/Comprehensive+). (p6 table and p35)

patches.rationale: Cruise on‑board medical/dental benefits are essentially medical and evacuation. Adding this alias aids consistent mapping of cruise medical lines to the medical_and_evacuation category.
patches.description: Add alias used in cruise benefit tables.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Cruise Cover (ii) On-board Medical and Dental Cover – Unlimited. (pp11, 42–45)
D.10 Optional: Cruise cover – extends existing medical cover to cruises. (p82)

patches.rationale: Both PDSs explicitly require purchasing a cruise option for ocean/sea cruises with overnight stays, and note situations where it is not required (e.g., river cruises, certain short or domestic waters). Clarifying this improves extraction consistency.
patches.description: Whether cruise-related claims require purchasing an add-on. true if the policy requires selecting and paying for a cruise option to enable cruise-related benefits (typically for ocean/sea cruises with overnight stays). Note common exceptions (e.g., river cruises, single-night cruises, ferries, certain Australian coastal/inland waters) when stated by the insurer.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: If Your cruise is on an ocean or sea ... You must tell Us You are doing a cruise and pay an extra premium ... Not needed for a river cruise, one-night cruise, ferries, certain Australian coastal/inland waters. (p11)
D.10 Optional: Cruise cover – add the cruise option (overnight in a cabin) and pay extra premium; cover then extends to cruises. (p82)
